# 1 Enoch Chapter 80 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn-astr (Aramaic) | **Section:** Astronomical Book (Book of Luminaries)

---

**1** Then Uriel the angel replied to me: "Enoch, I have shown you everything — I have revealed to you the sun and the moon, the star-leaders of heaven and all who set them in motion, their duties, their appointed times, and their departures."

**2** "But in the days of the sinners, the years will be cut short. Their crops will be slow to grow in their fields, and everything on earth will be disrupted — nothing will appear at its proper time. Rain will be withheld; the sky will hold it back.

**3** In those days, the earth's produce will be delayed and will not ripen when it should, and the fruit of the trees will not come at its appointed time.

**4** The moon will deviate from her regular order and not appear at her scheduled time.

**5** And in those days the sun will be seen traveling at evening along the outermost edge of his great chariot in the west, shining more brightly than his proper light allows.

**6** Many of the star-leaders will break the laws prescribed for them, altering their orbits and duties, failing to appear at their designated seasons.

**7** The whole ordered system of the stars will be hidden from the sinners. Those on earth will be confused by them, will lose their way entirely, and will go so far astray as to worship them as gods.

**8** Evil will multiply upon them, and punishment will come upon them to destroy them all."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Chapter 80 is the dark eschatological counterpart to the orderly cosmos of chapters 72-79. When sinners corrupt the world, the cosmic machinery itself breaks down: seasons fail, rain is withheld, stars leave their courses. The worst consequence is idolatry — people misread the disordered stars as gods (v. 7). This polemic against stellar worship was directly relevant in the Hellenistic period when astral religion was widespread.*
